\begin{quote}
\textbf{Common Values Linear Bidding:} Two players participate in a first-price sealed-bid auction in a common-values setting. The value of the good for each player is given by \(\theta_1 + \theta_2\), where \(\theta_i\) is a signal observed only by player \(i\) and is uniformly distributed over the interval \([0, 1]\). Hence if player \(i\) observes his signal \(\theta_i\) then his expected valuation is equal to \(0.5 + \theta_i\) (but unlike the previous exercise, this is a common-values setting).

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Show that there is a symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium in which each bidder \(i\)'s bidding strategy is of the form \(s_i^*(\theta_i) = a + b\theta_i\).
\item
  What is the expected payoff of a player if his type is \(\theta_i\)?
\item
  Show that for each value of \(\theta_i\) the equilibrium bid of player \(i\) is less than what you found in (a) of the previous exercise.
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
